Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

The imported “habsburg-netherlands” feature runs approximately 1530–1650, but northern provinces ceased to be ruled by Philip II during the revolt and became a separate Republic; southern territories remained under Habsburg rule after 1650. Imported borders are not independently verified.

Plantin-Moretus was an unusually successful urban family firm. Its practices cannot be generalized to all rural, poor or religiously diverse households; the Amsterdam cesspit example is northern. Narrative awaits independent review.

proposedOverrides.summary: The imported “Habsburg Netherlands” label covers about 1530 to 1650, but the Low Countries did not remain one political unit. Charles V passed rule to Philip II in 1555; revolt and the 1581 renunciation divided the north from the Habsburg south. Northern provinces formed a republic, while the south continued under Spanish Habsburg rule. Antwerp’s Plantin-Moretus workshop reveals family learning, women’s work, printing and illness amid war. The 1648 Peace of Münster recognized northern independence; the southern provinces continued beyond this map label’s 1650 endpoint.

identityEvidence.assessment: Imported label and interval confirmed; historic border accuracy unverified.
